finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated req.query.host value is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters (; | $() backticks &&) execute arbitrary commands as the server user.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP GET /ping query parameter, unauthenticated, attacker-controlled)
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which runs via /bin/sh -c

trace.note: GET /ping handler registered with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated into command string and passed to exec (shell)
command stdout returned to the attacker in the response, so output is exfiltrated directly

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or escaping on host; no authentication or authorization middleware; no use of execFile/argv array (unlike /version). Not a decoy: the input is not constant, unlike /uptime and /version. Express may also yield array/object for repeated or nested query params, which is coerced to string by concatenation. A value beginning with '-' also allows option injection even without shell metacharacters.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) in the /ping handler at tools.js:6, which has no auth or validation, and tools.js:11 returns stdout to the caller. Output only comes back when the command exits 0, which is easy to arrange (e.g. `127.0.0.1;id`).
